seoTitle: How to Link Confluence With Jira (Step-by-Step)
metaDescription: Connect Confluence and Jira so documentation, issues, and sprints stay linked, giving your team instant visibility into project progress.
intro: Keeping documentation separate from your issue tracker makes it easy for requirements and progress notes to fall out of sync. This guide walks through linking Confluence with Jira so your pages and issues reference each other directly, improving visibility for the whole team.

steps.heading: Confirm both tools are connected
steps.body: Since Jira and Confluence are both Atlassian products, make sure your site has both apps set up under the same Atlassian account.

steps.heading: Link a Confluence page to a Jira issue
steps.body: From within a Jira issue, use the link option to attach a related Confluence page, or insert a Jira issue macro directly into a Confluence page.

steps.heading: Use Confluence for project documentation
steps.body: Keep requirements, meeting notes, and specs in Confluence pages that are linked back to their relevant Jira epics or tickets.

steps.heading: Review links regularly
steps.body: Periodically check that linked pages and issues are still accurate as your project evolves, especially after sprint changes.

steps.heading: Apply team best practices
steps.body: Establish a simple convention, like linking every epic to its planning doc, so the Jira-Confluence connection stays consistent across projects.

faq.question: Do I need separate Confluence and Jira licenses?
faq.answer: Yes, Confluence and Jira are separate products, though many Atlassian plans bundle both under one site.

faq.question: Can I see linked Confluence pages from inside a Jira issue?
faq.answer: Yes, once linked, related Confluence pages show up directly in the issue's links section for quick access.

faq.question: Does linking sync content between the two tools?
faq.answer: No, linking just connects the issue and page so you can navigate between them — the content in each stays managed separately.

faq.question: Can this help with Agile reporting?
faq.answer: Yes, linking documentation to epics and stories gives your team instant context alongside sprint reports and boards.
